question: What is the primary law guiding nursing practice and training in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Public Service General Orders
options.B: Nigerian Medical and Dental Practitioners Act
options.C: National Health Insurance Authority Act
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Registration Act

explanation: This is the core law that established the nursing council and sets the legal boundaries for our practice in Nigeria.

question: At what fill level should a clinical waste bag be tied up and removed?

options.A: Completely packed to the brim
options.B: Whenever the shift ends
options.C: Three-quarters full
options.D: One-quarter full

explanation: Correct! Tying bags at 3/4 capacity stops them from overflowing, spilling, or tearing when you carry them. Stay safe out there!

question: When giving a bed bath, in what direction should you wash the skin?

options.A: From the feet up to the face
options.B: From dirtiest areas to cleanest areas
options.C: From the left side to the right side
options.D: From cleanest areas to dirtier areas

explanation: Brilliant! Moving from clean to dirty ensures you don't drag germs from lower areas up onto sensitive spots like the face.

question: What is a primary focus of health assessment in older adults?

options.A: Monitoring pediatric developmental milestones
options.B: Evaluating cognitive function and fall risks
options.C: Checking birth weight and Apgar scores
options.D: Screening exclusively for adolescent scoliosis

explanation: Older adults face unique age-related challenges like memory changes and balance issues that require targeted assessments. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which handy tool do home care nurses often use to help patients manage multiple daily pills?

options.A: Sterile wound dressing
options.B: Blood pressure cuff
options.C: Peak flow meter
options.D: Weekly pill organizer

explanation: A weekly pill box is a simple lifesaver! It sorts medications by days and times, helping patients stay on track.

question: How do modern apology laws treat expressions of sympathy from healthcare providers?

options.A: They remove all licensing requirements for doctors involved in adverse events
options.B: They force the hospital to pay double compensation in every civil lawsuit
options.C: They protect humanitarian expressions of sorrow from being used as evidence of fault
options.D: They make it illegal for any nurse to speak directly to a patient's family

explanation: Apology protection laws encourage honesty by making sure that showing human empathy and sorrow cannot be used in court as proof of guilt.

question: Why is it helpful for student nurses to understand research paradigms?

options.A: To evaluate published studies and choose proper evidence for care
options.B: To calculate exact medication dosages for surgical patients
options.C: To diagnose rare diseases using laboratory blood test results
options.D: To write hospital administration policies without clinical data

explanation: Knowing this helps you look at a research paper and figure out if the findings make sense and can actually help your patients on the ward.

question: What is the main reason we use electronic monitors in emergency and critical care?

options.A: To give permanent physical support to failing organs
options.B: To completely replace the need for physical nursing checks
options.C: To give out drugs automatically without any human check
options.D: To keep a continuous eye on vital signs in real time

explanation: Spot-checking is great, but monitors act like extra pairs of eyes, tracking vital signs constantly so we can catch sudden changes right away. You've got this!

question: What is a key sign of an authentic leader in clinical practice?

options.A: Hiding mistakes made by senior medical personnel
options.B: Pretending to have clinical skills one does not possess
options.C: Transparent, ethical behavior and genuine self-awareness
options.D: Focusing exclusively on financial profit for the hospital

explanation: Authentic leaders build real trust because they are honest, stay true to their ethics, and aren't afraid to be real with their team.

question: What is the outermost layer of the skin called?

options.A: Subcutaneous layer
options.B: Dermis
options.C: Hypodermis
options.D: Epidermis

explanation: The epidermis is the outermost, superficial layer of the skin made of epithelial tissue. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h1)

question: In infection control, what do we mean by a 'reservoir'?

options.A: The natural home where a microorganism lives and multiplies
options.B: The method by which a germ travels through the air
options.C: An opening where germs leave the human body
options.D: A person who is vulnerable to catching a disease

explanation: Think of a reservoir as a cozy hangout spot for germs—it could be a human, an animal, soil, or even equipment where they live and grow.

question: Why do we stress daily weight monitoring as a crucial self-care habit for heart failure patients?

options.A: It catches fluid retention and worsening heart failure early
options.B: It tells the patient exactly how many calories they burned
options.C: It replaces the need for measuring blood pressure daily
options.D: It measures the thickness of the left ventricular muscle

explanation: Spot on! Scales don't lie. A sudden weight gain over a day or two is often the very first warning sign that fluid is building up, long before severe breathlessness strikes.

question: Why is daily weight tracking important for a patient with heart failure on a sodium-restricted diet?

options.A: Sudden weight gain often signals dangerous fluid retention from excess salt
options.B: It measures how fast the patient's muscle mass is growing
options.C: It proves the patient is eating enough calories to prevent malnutrition
options.D: It determines the exact dosage of vitamins needed each week

explanation: Because water weight accumulates rapidly when sodium is high, daily scale readings give an early warning before severe symptoms appear. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h8)

question: Which of these signs is the classic giveaway that an IV has 'infiltrated' (leaked into the tissue)?

options.A: A warm, red, hard streak running all the way up the arm
options.B: Severe chest pain accompanied by audible lung crackles
options.C: Bright red bleeding gushing out around the plastic catheter
options.D: Swelling, coolness, and pallor around the insertion site

explanation: Spot on! When IV fluid leaks into the tissue instead of the vein, it makes the skin look pale, feel cool, and swell up. Time to restart the line!

question: What is the preferred method for first-trimester uterine evacuation in post-abortion care?

options.A: High-dose oral oxytocin alone
options.B: Manual vacuum aspiration
options.C: Sharp metallic curettage without anesthesia
options.D: Major open abdominal surgery

explanation: Well done! Manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) is widely preferred because it is safe, highly effective, and much gentler than older methods.

question: Why don't we use syrup of ipecac anymore to treat poisoning?

options.A: It is too expensive to manufacture
options.B: It causes unpredictable vomiting and risks aspiration
options.C: It permanently stains the lining of the stomach
options.D: It neutralizes all known hospital antidotes

explanation: Ipecac causes vomiting at random, delayed times. If the patient vomits and breathes it into their lungs (aspiration), it can cause serious damage, so it's a no-go today.

question: As a nurse, what is an essential step when assessing a patient who might have a contagious infection?

options.A: Taking a detailed history of recent travel, occupation, and contacts
options.B: Isolating the patient in a surgical suite immediately
options.C: Measuring the patient's blood pressure every fifteen minutes
options.D: Administering broad-spectrum antibiotics before checking lab results

explanation: You're building great clinical detective skills! Asking about travel, work, and who they've been around helps track down where the bug came from.

question: When can palliative care be introduced during the course of a serious illness?

options.A: At any stage alongside life-prolonging treatments
options.B: Exclusively after all curative options have failed
options.C: Only when the patient is discharged back home
options.D: Only during the final twenty-four hours of life

explanation: Palliative care is not just for end-of-life; it can and should be integrated early alongside disease-modifying or curative treatments. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which of these is an UNSAFE way to thaw frozen meat?

options.A: Using the defrost setting on a microwave oven
options.B: Submerging it securely in cold running tap water
options.C: Leaving it on the kitchen counter at room temperature
options.D: Thawing it slowly inside the refrigerator compartment

explanation: You nailed it! Leaving meat on the counter lets the outside warm up into the danger zone where bacteria love to multiply.

question: A community health nurse is planning a cervical cancer screening outreach. Which test is she most likely to utilize?

options.A: Liver biopsy
options.B: Chest X-ray
options.C: Pap smear
options.D: Prostate-specific antigen test

explanation: A Pap smear is a standard, widely used screening tool for detecting cervical cell abnormalities and precancerous lesions. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which client situation puts them at the highest danger if a fire breaks out at home?

options.A: Living in a single-story bungalow
options.B: Using a standard landline telephone
options.C: Having pale skin and light-colored hair
options.D: Severe mobility impairments preventing quick movement

explanation: If a patient cannot walk or move on their own, they depend completely on you or others to get them out safely.

question: What is an important duty of a community health nurse when dealing with voluntary agencies?

options.A: Referring vulnerable patients to appropriate agency programs
options.B: Managing the global headquarters of faith-based charities
options.C: Auditing the financial tax accounts of all international donors
options.D: Passing new national legislation for non-profit groups

explanation: Correct! As a nurse, knowing what local agencies offer helps you connect your patients to free or low-cost support outside the hospital.

question: What is the simple difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine separates exposed people
options.B: Isolation is used for animals, while quarantine is used for humans
options.C: Quarantine involves drug treatment, while isolation only uses herbal remedies
options.D: Quarantine is voluntary, while isolation is always illegal

explanation: Easy to remember: Isolation keeps already sick people away from others, while quarantine holds people who were exposed just to see if they fall ill.

question: Why is keeping our environment clean considered a primary defense against diseases?

options.A: It permanently alters the genetic makeup of pathogens so they become harmless
options.B: It ensures that community members never come into contact with wild animals
options.C: It replaces the need for any form of medical treatment during disease outbreaks
options.D: It removes the breeding grounds and shelter that vectors and pests need to survive

explanation: You got it! A clean environment denies pests the food, water, and shelter they need to multiply.

question: When should discharge planning ideally start for a patient admitted to a rehab unit?

options.A: Forty-eight hours before leaving
options.B: Only after therapy is finished
options.C: On the day of admission
options.D: When the patient asks to go home

explanation: Starting discharge planning on day one ensures family training and home changes are sorted out smoothly without last-minute panic.

question: What is the big superpower of adaptive immunity compared to innate immunity?

options.A: It requires no cellular involvement to neutralize foreign agents
options.B: It responds instantly within seconds of the very first infection
options.C: It relies solely on physical barriers like the skin and mucous
options.D: It develops long-term immunological memory for specific pathogens

explanation: Adaptive immunity keeps a memory of past infections. That way, if the same germ attacks again, your body mounts a much stronger and faster defense!

question: What is the medical term for difficulty swallowing?

options.A: Deglutition
options.B: Aspiration
options.C: Dysphagia
options.D: Peristalsis

explanation: Dysphagia is the clinical term used when a patient experiences trouble moving food or liquid from the mouth to the stomach safely. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h1)

question: Why is it often hard to tell exactly when someone caught leprosy?

options.A: It takes a very long time for signs to show up
options.B: Early symptoms always go away on their own
options.C: It spreads through dirty drinking water
options.D: The bacteria die instantly outside the body

explanation: Because symptoms can take months or even years to appear, it is tough to trace back the exact moment of exposure. Don't worry, you're learning!

question: Which parts of the body are mainly affected by leprosy?

options.A: Bones and joints
options.B: Liver and gut
options.C: Skin and peripheral nerves
options.D: Lungs and upper airways

explanation: The leprosy bacteria love cooler areas of the body, which is why they mainly attack the skin and the nerves outside the brain and spinal cord. You've got this!

question: Why must community nurses look beyond the clinic when dealing with poor nutrition?

options.A: Because nutrition problems only exist inside large hospital wards
options.B: Because hospital management forbids nurses from talking about food
options.C: Because clinical medications can cure malnutrition completely on their own
options.D: Because root causes like poverty and food disruption require community-based action

explanation: Spot on! Nutritional challenges are often tied to bigger social and economic issues. Giving medicine alone isn't enough—we need community action and education too.

question: Which common condition involves the weakening of bone due to rapid mineral loss from the spongy trabeculae?

options.A: Osteoporosis
options.B: Osteomyelitis
options.C: Osteoarthritis
options.D: Osteosarcoma

explanation: You've got this! Osteoporosis means 'porous bones.' It happens when bones lose minerals too quickly, making the tiny spongy struts thin out and break easily.

question: How do hospital policies directly help keep patients safe?

options.A: By ensuring that patients pay their hospital bills on time
options.B: By increasing the number of visiting hours for relatives
options.C: By reducing the paperwork required for nursing handovers
options.D: By embedding evidence-based best practices into daily routines

explanation: Policies translate proven safety research into practical, everyday steps that protect our patients from harm.

question: Why do nurses look at reproductive health as a lifelong journey rather than just a passing phase?

options.A: Because reproductive needs change and persist from birth to old age
options.B: Because healthcare funding is tied to lifelong patient monitoring
options.C: Because reproductive organs never undergo natural degeneration
options.D: Because patients only seek care during their childbearing years

explanation: Spot on! Reproductive health matters at every single stage of life, meaning our care and guidance as nurses never truly stop.

question: Why must reusable equipment like stethoscopes be wiped with disinfectant between patients?

options.A: To prevent cross-contamination and hospital-acquired infections
options.B: To keep the metal parts from rusting in humid weather
options.C: To remove any manufacturer dust from the surface
options.D: To ensure the sound quality remains clear for hearing

explanation: Medical tools can easily carry germs from one patient to another if they are not cleaned properly. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h3)

question: How does psychoeducation help a struggling family during a medical crisis?

options.A: It replaces the need for doctors to talk to the patient
options.B: It reduces anxiety caused by the unknown by explaining the condition
options.C: It completely pays off all accumulated hospital and pharmacy bills
options.D: It forces family members to hide their true feelings from staff

explanation: Providing clear, understandable information about a disease helps families feel more prepared and less frightened about what to expect. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is the main goal of the intensive phase of TB treatment?

options.A: To test if the patient is allergic to all four drugs
options.B: To rapidly reduce the bacterial load and stop infectiousness
options.C: To rebuild the damaged lung tissue back to normal
options.D: To completely finish the entire course of treatment

explanation: Hitting TB hard with four drugs quickly drops the germ count so the patient stops spreading it to others. Excellent clinical milestone!

question: What is another common name for incidence density?

options.A: Cumulative prevalence
options.B: Point mortality rate
options.C: Person-time incidence
options.D: Case fatality ratio

explanation: Incidence density is also known as person-time incidence because it tracks the actual time units each person contributes to the study. You're mastering the terminology!

question: Which food items do patients most often forget to mention during a diet recall?

options.A: Main staple foods like rice and yams
options.B: Prescribed liquid meal supplements
options.C: Large portions of hospital breakfast
options.D: Snacks, sauces, and sugary drinks

explanation: It's easy to forget small bites and sips! Extra snacks, drinks, and cooking oils are the most commonly missed items.

question: What is a common medication-related cause of falls in older adults?

options.A: Mild skin irritation from ointments
options.B: Dry mouth from antibiotic use
options.C: Dizziness from blood pressure drugs
options.D: Increased appetite from vitamins

explanation: Medications that lower blood pressure can cause sudden dizziness when a person stands up, leading to a fall. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of teaching communities about infection control?

options.A: To empower patients with practical knowledge to protect themselves
options.B: To eliminate all microorganisms from the environment
options.C: To replace the need for professional medical diagnosis
options.D: To ensure patients never leave their homes

explanation: Knowledge is power! When we educate our communities, we give people the tools to keep themselves and their families safe.

question: Why does the biopsychosocial model work best for explaining drug addiction?

options.A: It focuses solely on the patient's current environmental stress
options.B: It looks at biological, psychological, and social factors together
options.C: It relies entirely on psychiatric medication history
options.D: It proves that genetics is the only true cause of drug use

explanation: Addiction is complex, and the biopsychosocial model acknowledges that body chemistry, mental health, and life surroundings all contribute. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h4)

question: What triggers the physical changes of puberty?

options.A: Hormonal surges from the endocrine system
options.B: Sudden changes in environmental temperature
options.C: Rapid expansion of skeletal muscle mass
options.D: Increased intake of dietary proteins

explanation: Puberty kicks off when the brain sends signals to the endocrine system to release hormones that drive body changes.

question: What does it mean if a placenta is described as a 'battledore placenta'?

options.A: A placenta with a thick white ring on its edge
options.B: A placenta split into two equal-sized lobes
options.C: A placenta where the umbilical cord inserts at the margin
options.D: A placenta with an accessory lobe nearby

explanation: Think of a battledore insertion like a tennis racket handle attached right at the edge of the disk instead of the middle. Easy to picture once you see it! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h2)

question: You notice a patient has dry, brittle hair, pale skin, and spoon-shaped nails. What part of the nutritional assessment is this?

options.A: Dietary history recall
options.B: Clinical observations
options.C: Biochemical tests
options.D: Anthropometric tracking

explanation: When you look directly at the patient's body for physical signs of nutrition issues, you are doing a clinical observation!

question: What does the term 'morbidity' mean in community health?

options.A: The percentage of literate adults
options.B: The state of being unhealthy or diseased
options.C: The total number of deaths in a year
options.D: The rate of migration into a rural area

explanation: Morbidity describes illness, sickness, or the presence of disease within a population, separate from mortality which refers to death. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why do healthcare teams hold professional meetings?

options.A: Coordination and clinical updates among staff
options.B: Evaluating individual nurses on daily bedside tasks
options.C: Replacing all written forms of hospital communication
options.D: Providing a space for extended social interactions

explanation: Meetings bring everyone together to align patient care and share important updates. You'll see this often on the ward!

question: What is the main job of minerals like sodium and potassium in our bodies?

options.A: Storing excess kilocalories for times of fasting
options.B: Regulating fluid balance and nerve transmission
options.C: Acting as primary structural units for muscle fibers
options.D: Providing the main source of daily cellular energy

explanation: Spot on! Sodium and potassium are key electrolytes that keep our fluids balanced and help nerves send signals to muscles.

question: Do retrospective studies that only use old patient charts still need ethical approval?

options.A: No, because the patients have already been discharged
options.B: Only if the study is funded by a pharmaceutical company
options.C: Yes, approval from an ethics committee or IRB is still required
options.D: Only if more than one thousand charts are reviewed

explanation: Spot on! Even though the patients aren't actively in the hospital anymore, their health information is still private and protected, so ethical clearance is a must.

question: Which cranial nerve mainly carries signals from the airways to the cough center in the brain?

options.A: Hypoglossal nerve
options.B: Facial nerve
options.C: Vagus nerve
options.D: Optic nerve

explanation: The vagus nerve acts like the main highway, carrying sensory signals straight from your lungs and airways up to the cough center in the brain. Great job remembering your cranial nerves!

question: After a very tough loss on the children's ward, what best helps the nursing team cope with the stress?

options.A: Forcing the team to take on extra admissions to stay busy
options.B: Pretending the event did not happen to maintain normal routines
options.C: Punishing the nurses immediately for failing to save the patient
options.D: Providing a safe space for structured team debriefing and counseling

explanation: Talking through grief together in a supportive session helps nurses heal and prevents long-term emotional burnout.

question: How do rude or unsupportive ward staff affect student nurses?

options.A: They automatically boost your exam grades
options.B: They lower your confidence and make you scared to ask questions
options.C: They have zero impact on how well you perform
options.D: They force you to study better on your own

explanation: A toxic ward atmosphere makes students fearful and hesitant, which slows down learning. A supportive team makes all the difference!

question: Which condition often develops later if obsessive-compulsive neurosis is left untreated?

options.A: Antisocial personality disorder
options.B: Schizoaffective disorder
options.C: Major depressive disorder
options.D: Dissociative identity disorder

explanation: You got it! Dealing with constant anxiety and exhaustion day after day often leads to clinical depression down the line.

question: Which part of the female reproductive organ is affected by cervical cancer?

options.A: The lower part of the uterus
options.B: The external folds of the labia majora
options.C: The muscular walls of the fallopian tubes
options.D: The inner lining of the ovarian cortex

explanation: Great job! Cervical cancer happens right in the cervix, which is the lower, narrow neck of the uterus connecting to the vagina. You've got this!

question: A patient is given timolol eye drops for glaucoma. How do these drops actually lower eye pressure?

options.A: By dissolving protein deposits on the clear cornea
options.B: By widening the tear drainage system
options.C: By completely relaxing the outer eye muscles
options.D: By decreasing the production of fluid (aqueous humor)

explanation: Timolol is a beta-blocker. It tells the ciliary body to slow down on making fluid (aqueous humor), which lowers the pressure inside the eye. Neat, right?

question: How does severe income inequality affect the overall health of a population?

options.A: It eliminates chronic stress among lower-income earners.
options.B: It completely stops the spread of infectious diseases.
options.C: It places a heavy disease burden on poorer groups who cannot afford early care.
options.D: It ensures that everyone has equal access to private clinics.

explanation: Wide gaps in wealth mean poorer citizens cannot afford preventive care or early treatment, allowing minor sicknesses to develop into severe, chronic illnesses. [learn more](GST322_U3_T7#GST322_U3_T7_h2)

question: During the movement called flexion, what happens to the baby's chin?

options.A: It remains extended away from the body
options.B: It rotates fully toward the left hip
options.C: It points upward toward the maternal spine
options.D: It is pushed down to touch the chest

explanation: Correct! As the baby moves down, resistance from the pelvis makes the chin tuck neatly right against the chest.

question: Why does wearing the correct glove size matter so much in clinical work?

options.A: It prevents tearing and keeps your fingers nimble
options.B: It stops the material from causing latex allergies
options.C: It keeps the gloves completely sterile
options.D: It means you don't have to wash your hands afterwards

explanation: Gloves that are too tight will easily rip, while oversized gloves make it hard to grip things. Finding your right size is key!

question: When are transmission-based precautions added to patient care?

options.A: Only after laboratory tests prove the patient is cured
options.B: When the hospital runs out of standard gloves
options.C: When a specific contagious disease is suspected or confirmed
options.D: Whenever a visitor enters the isolation room

explanation: Transmission-based precautions are extra steps added on top of standard rules when dealing with specific, easily spread germs. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h4)

question: A new mother looks pale, feels dizzy, and her pad is soaked with bright red blood within 20 minutes. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Assess the uterine fundus for tone and massage if boggy
options.B: Wait until the scheduled six-week postnatal checkup
options.C: Tell the mother to walk around the room to improve circulation
options.D: Encourage the mother to drink large volumes of cold water

explanation: Great clinical thinking! These are classic signs of postpartum hemorrhage. Checking and massaging the uterus helps it contract and stops the bleeding.

question: Why is paying out-of-pocket for medical care at the hospital dangerous for families?

options.A: It increases the cost of medical equipment
options.B: It prevents nurses from administering medications
options.C: It forces families into sudden poverty during health emergencies
options.D: It causes hospitals to close down immediately

explanation: You've got this! Paying directly for care on the spot can wipe out family savings and delay the care someone desperately needs. That's why health financing matters so much.

question: Who should be targeted as key stakeholders during this step of mobilisation?

options.A: Foreign tourists visiting the local market
options.B: National politicians running for high office
options.C: International pharmaceutical company executives
options.D: Religious leaders, women's heads, and youth representatives

explanation: Local leaders hold immense influence over community behavior and are vital partners for driving health initiatives. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h4)

question: What is usually one of the very first warning signs a woman might notice with cervical cancer?

options.A: Severe lower abdominal pain during ovulation
options.B: Complete cessation of all menstrual periods
options.C: Abnormal vaginal bleeding after sexual intercourse
options.D: Sudden and unexplained rapid weight gain

explanation: Spot on! Bleeding after sex (post-coital spotting) or irregular bleeding is a classic sign because the abnormal tissue on the cervix is very fragile and easily irritated.

question: Which vitamin is often given alongside isoniazid to protect a patient's nerves?

options.A: Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3)
options.B: Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6)
options.C: Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C)
options.D: Tocopherol (Vitamin E)

explanation: Isoniazid can drain Vitamin B6 levels, leading to tingling or nerve pain. Adding Vitamin B6 prevents this pesky side effect.

question: What is a big clinical plus of using biphasic defibrillators over monophasic ones?

options.A: They automatically treat both shockable and non-shockable rhythms
options.B: They achieve success with lower energy levels and less tissue injury
options.C: They do not require any conductive gel pads on the chest
options.D: They can deliver shocks safely through wet clothing

explanation: Because biphasic shocks work so well, we don't need as much electricity. This keeps the patient safer by lowering the risk of skin burns and heart muscle damage.

question: Why is it so important to involve the community at every single stage of a health program?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for baseline surveys
options.B: It allows the government to avoid paying health workers
options.C: It ensures interventions address real, locally felt needs
options.D: It speeds up the construction of primary health centers

explanation: Spot on! When locals help plan from day one, we make sure we are actually solving the problems they care about most, rather than guessing what they need.

question: A community clinic wants to stop teenagers from dropping out of care. What should they do first?

options.A: Require formal written permission from local chiefs
options.B: Move the clinic to a remote location outside the city
options.C: Offer drop-in services and reduce long waiting times
options.D: Increase fees to cover new facility decorations

explanation: Spot on! Cutting down long delays and allowing flexible drop-in visits keeps young people engaged and willing to return.

question: What is a major risk associated with using social media networks during a fast-moving crisis?

options.A: The rapid spread of unverified rumors and false information
options.B: High costs charged to citizens for reading emergency alerts
options.C: The complete inability to transmit text messages or pictures
options.D: Government blockades that stop all communication instantly

explanation: Social media allows anyone to post instantly, which can lead to panic if false reports circulate before officials verify them. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T9#GNS315_U5_T9_h5)

question: What is the nurse's main role when it comes to informed consent?

options.A: Writing the medical prescription for the diagnostic procedure
options.B: Explaining the legal liability of the hospital to the family
options.C: Deciding whether the patient is well enough to undergo the test
options.D: Ensuring the patient understands the procedure and has signed voluntarily

explanation: Well done! The nurse makes sure the patient truly gets what the doctor explained and is agreeing of their own free will—no pressure!

question: According to the Transtheoretical Model, what is the very first stage of behavioural change?

options.A: Preparation
options.B: Maintenance
options.C: Action
options.D: Precontemplation

explanation: Correct! In the precontemplation stage, a person isn't thinking about changing yet, and might not even see that there is a problem.

question: What is the main goal of medication reconciliation during a patient's hospital stay?

options.A: To reduce the number of nurses required on duty
options.B: To return unused drugs back to the pharmaceutical company
options.C: To calculate the total cost of drugs used in the ward
options.D: To compare past and current medications to prevent errors

explanation: Medication reconciliation ensures that home medications and new hospital orders match properly without dangerous gaps or overlaps. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h4)

question: What do geographical boundaries (like rivers or roads) give to a traditional community?

options.A: Clear physical limits and a defined space for service delivery
options.B: Guaranteed financial funding from international agencies
options.C: Absolute immunity from infectious disease outbreaks
options.D: Complete isolation from neighboring populations

explanation: Physical borders make it easy for nurses to map out an area and plan where to bring healthcare services.

question: Why is a pelvic ultrasound ordered for a patient with severe pelvic pain and suspected oophoritis?

options.A: To look at the ovaries and check for abscesses or fluid
options.B: To completely replace the need for a physical exam
options.C: To check the length of the patient's menstrual cycle
options.D: To measure exact hormone levels in the blood

explanation: Ultrasounds give us a clear 'window' inside the pelvis to spot structural changes or dangerous pockets of fluid like abscesses.

question: What should every good IEC material clearly include at the end of its message?

options.A: A detailed biography of the nurse who designed the material
options.B: A specific call to action telling the audience what to do next
options.C: A complete list of medical research references and journal sources
options.D: A complex scientific definition of the disease being discussed

explanation: Always tell your audience what practical step they can take right now to protect their health!

question: Why do nurses apply an ice pack to the perineum right after a vaginal delivery?

options.A: To speed up the return of lochia alba
options.B: To reduce localized swelling and numb pain
options.C: To prevent the uterus from becoming boggy
options.D: To stimulate early bowel movements

explanation: Ice is wonderful here! It narrows the blood vessels, which quickly brings down swelling and helps numb the area so the mother feels more comfortable.

question: Which medical condition is closely linked to blood vessel smooth muscle staying too constricted over time?

options.A: Osteoporosis
options.B: Anemia
options.C: Hypertension
options.D: Hypoglycemia

explanation: When the smooth muscle in blood vessel walls stays chronically tight, the vessels narrow and resistance climbs, which we know as high blood pressure (hypertension). Great job working through this set!

question: What is the main reason we use the coefficient of variation in research?

options.A: Calculating the exact sample size needed for a nursing study
options.B: Comparing variability between data sets with different units or means
options.C: Finding the absolute middle value of a skewed distribution
options.D: Eliminating all extreme outliers from a clinical data set

explanation: When comparing things measured in totally different ways (like age in years vs. weight in kg), the coefficient of variation helps us put them on a fair playing field.

question: How do lab staff figure out if an antibiotic can kill a specific bacterium on a test plate?

options.A: By counting how many days the culture plate sat inside the incubator
options.B: By observing if the entire agar plate changes to a bright red color
options.C: By checking the expiration date printed on the exterior box of disks
options.D: By measuring the clear ring of no growth around the antibiotic disk

explanation: That clear halo around the antibiotic disk is called the zone of inhibition. The bigger the ring, the better the drug works!

question: Which of the following is a common management challenge in day care centres?

options.A: Complete absence of any government regulations
options.B: Too much space for very few enrolled children
options.C: High staff turnover and inadequate funding
options.D: Excessive numbers of trained medical doctors on site

explanation: Many day care centres struggle with financial constraints and frequent changes in caregiving staff, which can disrupt service quality. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h7)

question: Why do nurses stick around and monitor a patient for about 30 minutes after certain shots or vaccines?

options.A: To ensure the patient does not walk around too soon
options.B: To verify that the medication has been fully absorbed
options.C: To measure the exact change in body temperature
options.D: To watch for acute allergic or anaphylactic reactions

explanation: Better safe than sorry! Severe allergic reactions usually pop up fast. Keeping an eye on your patient during that first half-hour means you can jump in with emergency help if needed.

question: Which nerve carries visual signals from the eye to the brain?

options.A: The auditory nerve
options.B: The trigeminal nerve
options.C: The oculomotor nerve
options.D: The optic nerve

explanation: The optic nerve acts like a data cable, carrying all the visual messages from the back of your eye straight to the brain.

question: What is the final goal of the blood clotting (coagulation) cascade?

options.A: Breakdown of mature red blood cells by spleen macrophages
options.B: Conversion of soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin threads
options.C: Release of erythropoietin from the renal cortex
options.D: Rapid constriction of smooth muscle in the heart ventricles

explanation: Brilliant! The whole clotting chain reaction ends by turning liquid fibrinogen into a tough, solid net of fibrin fibers that seals up the cut.

question: Why do we need a whole team (doctors, nurses, social workers) to plan for psychiatric parole?

options.A: Different experts cover medical, social, legal, and daily living needs.
options.B: It ensures that doctors make all decisions without input from other staff.
options.C: Courts legally require at least ten different signatures for a discharge.
options.D: It slows down the release process so patients stay in the hospital longer.

explanation: Exactly! Reintegrating into society isn't just about medicine; patients need help with housing, legal steps, and daily support, which takes a whole team.

question: What happens if the body fails to maintain proper immune tolerance?

options.A: Innate barriers permanently lose their ability to secrete mucus
options.B: Primary lymphoid organs immediately stop producing white blood cells
options.C: The immune system attacks the body's own healthy cells and tissues
options.D: The body becomes completely defenseless against minor viral colds

explanation: Correct! When tolerance fails, the body stops recognizing 'self' and starts an autoimmune attack on its own healthy organs.

question: A father is admitted for chronic hypertension. Why should the nurse involve his spouse and children in his discharge education?

options.A: Family members must take over the patient's job responsibilities
options.B: Hospital regulations require at least three visitors per patient
options.C: It prevents the patient from speaking to the doctor alone
options.D: The family functions as a unit, and lifestyle changes require household support

explanation: Diet and lifestyle changes are much easier to maintain when the whole family understands and participates in them. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the main goal of palliative care when dealing with advanced breast cancer?

options.A: To train the patient to perform clinical breast exams on others
options.B: To reverse the side effects of prior chemotherapy drugs
options.C: To improve quality of life and relieve distressing symptoms
options.D: To completely cure the metastatic cancer cells in the bones

explanation: When a cure isn't possible anymore, palliative care steps in to wrap the patient in comfort, pain relief, and dignity.

question: Why are interdisciplinary rounds (where different health workers meet together) so helpful?

options.A: They ensure that doctors make all decisions without input from nurses
options.B: They allow multiple departments to discuss care plans together in real time
options.C: They remove the need for any documentation in the patient chart
options.D: They replace the nursing management team with administrative staff

explanation: Brilliant! Bringing everyone together at once clears up confusion instantly so the whole healthcare team is on the exact same page for the patient.

question: How many minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise are generally recommended per week for cardiovascular health?

options.A: At least 75 minutes
options.B: At least 150 minutes
options.C: At least 500 minutes
options.D: At least 300 minutes

explanation: Standard health guidelines recommend a minimum of 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity weekly to maintain heart health and lower disease risk. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h4)

question: A 16-year-old girl visits the clinic showing signs of severe mood swings and sudden weight loss. What should you, as the nurse, suspect first?

options.A: Emerging psychosocial or mental health challenges typical of this age group
options.B: Normal age-related cognitive decline
options.C: Permanent physical disability from birth
options.D: Early onset geriatric syndrome

explanation: Well done! Teens experiencing emotional stress often show it through sudden changes in behavior, body image concerns, or physical symptoms. Always keep an eye out for their mental wellbeing.

question: What is a vector in the context of disease transmission?

options.A: A living organism, usually an insect, that carries a pathogen to a host
options.B: An open skin lesion that allows bacteria to enter the bloodstream
options.C: A drug resistant bacterial strain found in hospital wards
options.D: A contaminated hospital instrument used on multiple patients

explanation: Vectors are living carriers like mosquitoes, ticks, or fleas that transfer infectious agents from one animal or human to another. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h6)

question: A nursing mother refuses to take her sick child to the clinic because the nearest facility is across a flooded river with no bridge. What primary factor is affecting her health behaviour?

options.A: A lack of personal intelligence
options.B: Stubborn defiance against modern medicine
options.C: An allergic reaction to clinic drugs
options.D: Structural and environmental barriers

explanation: This isn't about her willingness—it's a physical hurdle! Bad roads, long distances, and missing bridges are structural and environmental challenges. You're learning to look at the bigger picture in public health.

question: Why do STI infections in the male urethra often lead to swelling and pus?

options.A: The body produces extra oil to protect the skin from dryness
options.B: White blood cells rush to the invasion site to fight the microbes
options.C: Urine mixes with blood cells to create a protective barrier
options.D: Microbes block normal urine flow and cause back pressure

explanation: Think of white blood cells as your body's emergency responders. When germs attack, they flood the area to fight back, creating that pus we see in infections.

question: What biological process mainly causes the sudden height increase (growth spurt) during puberty?

options.A: The stretching of skin cells due to increased daily water intake
options.B: A sudden decrease in physical activity during school hours
options.C: A temporary failure of the pituitary gland to release hormones
options.D: Sex hormones interacting with growth hormone to lengthen bones

explanation: You got it! Rising sex hormones team up with growth hormone to help bones lengthen quickly during the adolescent growth spurt.

question: A patient drinks a six-ounce cup of juice. How many milliliters should the nurse record on the chart?

options.A: 60 milliliters
options.B: 180 milliliters
options.C: 300 milliliters
options.D: 120 milliliters

explanation: Multiplying six ounces by thirty milliliters per ounce gives a total volume of 180 milliliters. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h6)

question: When blood spins in a centrifuge, a tiny middle layer forms between the plasma and red blood cells. What is this 'buffy coat' made of?

options.A: Red blood cells and plasma
options.B: White blood cells and platelets
options.C: Dissolved proteins and electrolytes
options.D: Water and mineral salts

explanation: You got it! That thin buffy coat mainly contains your infection-fighting white blood cells and tiny platelets that help blood to clot.

question: Why is sharing login passwords with a colleague considered a serious breach of EHR security?

options.A: It automatically deletes all lab results stored in the database
options.B: It compromises accountability and violates patient confidentiality
options.C: It increases the hospital's monthly internet subscription fee
options.D: It causes the computer screen to freeze and crash completely

explanation: Audit trails link actions to specific user accounts; sharing credentials makes it impossible to know who actually accessed or changed a record. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h7)

question: How does hematogenous osteomyelitis differ from contiguous osteomyelitis?

options.A: Hematogenous spreads through the blood from another body site, while contiguous enters from direct contact with an outside source
options.B: Hematogenous is caused exclusively by viruses, while contiguous is bacterial
options.C: Hematogenous heals on its own without drugs, while contiguous requires amputation
options.D: Hematogenous only affects children, while contiguous only affects elderly patients

explanation: Hematogenous osteomyelitis travels via the bloodstream from a distant infection, whereas contiguous osteomyelitis spreads from a nearby wound, ulcer, or surgery. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h4)

question: What happens if hazardous waste accidentally gets thrown into the same bin as ordinary office paper?

options.A: The local municipal workers will sort it out safely at the dump
options.B: The total volume of waste instantly decreases by half
options.C: The entire combined batch must be treated as hazardous waste
options.D: The office paper automatically sterilizes the hazardous waste

explanation: Once clean and hazardous waste mix, you can no longer separate them safely. The whole bag now has to be treated as hazardous waste, which costs more and increases risk!

question: What do we call the routine choices you make using already established hospital rules and procedures?

options.A: Non-programmed choices
options.B: Programmed choices
options.C: Operational choices
options.D: Strategic choices

explanation: Programmed choices are your go-to solutions for familiar, everyday situations where a clear hospital guideline already exists.

question: Why does the pancreas release bicarbonate ions into the small intestine?

options.A: To stimulate the gallbladder to release stored bile
options.B: To neutralize acidic chyme coming from the stomach
options.C: To break down complex proteins into amino acids
options.D: To lower blood sugar levels after a heavy meal

explanation: Food coming from the stomach is super acidic. The pancreas sends out bicarbonate (think of it like natural baking soda) to calm down that acid so it doesn't burn your intestines!

question: What is the main energy source for a healthy, resting heart?

options.A: Glycogen stores
options.B: Amino acids
options.C: Blood urea nitrogen
options.D: Fatty acids

explanation: Even though glucose gets a lot of attention, your resting heart actually prefers burning fatty acids for its daily energy!

question: Which part of the Y-shaped antibody molecule binds directly to the antigen?

options.A: Complement tail
options.B: Fc region
options.C: Heavy chain stem
options.D: Fab region

explanation: Think of the Fab region as the hands of the antibody! The tips of the Y-shape have variable sequences that specifically match and grab onto antigens. You've got this!

question: Which management theory assumes that employees dislike work and must be tightly controlled?

options.A: Systems theory
options.B: Theory Y
options.C: Theory X
options.D: Virtue ethics

explanation: Theory X is the pessimistic view of workers—it assumes people are lazy, want to avoid responsibility, and need a strict boss watching their every move.

question: What is the main way hormonal contraceptives work in the body?

options.A: To speed up the fertilization process in the fallopian tubes
options.B: To mimic natural feedback loops and halt the release of eggs
options.C: To permanently destroy the reproductive organs of a patient
options.D: To increase the natural production of estrogen in the ovaries

explanation: You've got this! Hormonal contraceptives use synthetic hormones to gently trick the body's natural feedback system so that ovulation (releasing an egg) doesn't happen.

question: What do we call the process of forming mature sperm cells in the male testes?

options.A: Fertilization
options.B: Spermatogenesis
options.C: Gastrulation
options.D: Oogenesis

explanation: Spermatogenesis is just the medical term for how sperm cells are made in the testes. Think: 'spermato-' for sperm and '-genesis' for creation!

question: What was a major legal outcome of the Nancy Cruzan case regarding end-of-life care?

options.A: It established the need for clear evidence of a patient's prior treatment wishes
options.B: It created the very first living will document in history
options.C: It gave physicians the final say in removing feeding tubes
options.D: It banned families from ever stopping life support

explanation: The Supreme Court ruled that states could require clear and convincing evidence of what the patient would have wanted before stopping life support. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h2)

question: Why do rehabilitation nursing goals need to be specific and measurable?

options.A: To ensure that all patients achieve the exact same recovery speed
options.B: To satisfy legal requirements for hospital discharge paperwork
options.C: To clearly track patient progress and know when goals are met
options.D: To prevent the patient from participating in care planning

explanation: Clear goals let the whole healthcare team see if the patient is improving and if the nursing care plan is working well.

question: Why are vasodilators frequently used in managing severe heart complications?

options.A: They widen blood vessels to reduce the resistance the heart must fight against
options.B: They make the heart beat at maximum speed instantly
options.C: They thicken the blood to raise blood pressure
options.D: They make blood clot much faster

explanation: Imagine trying to push water through a pinched garden hose vs. a wide-open pipe. Vasodilators open up the blood vessels, making it much easier for a tired heart to push blood forward!

question: Why is active observation of a patient's reaction to hospital routines useful for assessing personality?

options.A: It automatically cures any hidden psychiatric disorders the patient has
options.B: It reveals how the person naturally copes with stress and interacts with others
options.C: It replaces the need to ever check vital signs or laboratory blood work
options.D: It gives the nurse exact proof of the patient's genetic family tree

explanation: Watching how patients handle routine stress and staff interactions highlights their underlying coping and relational styles. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T8#GNS314_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is the main goal of health insurance schemes like the NHIA?

options.A: To provide free international travel for senior nurses
options.B: To guarantee large profits for private insurance companies
options.C: To eliminate the need for doctors in primary health centers
options.D: To pool financial risks and reduce out-of-pocket spending

explanation: Insurance pools everyone's contributions together so that when someone falls sick, they don't have to pay massive cash on the spot.

question: When reading ingredient labels, which suffix usually tells you an ingredient is a sugar?

options.A: -ase
options.B: -ose
options.C: -ite
options.D: -one

explanation: Spotting a sneaky sugar is easier when you know the language! Most simple sugars end in '-ose', like sucrose, lactose, and glucose.

question: How should nurses view community challenges like poverty and lack of education when looking at health risks?

options.A: As permanent problems that public health programs can never fix
options.B: As important warning signs to help us protect vulnerable people
options.C: As proof that a specific person will definitely commit a crime
options.D: As minor issues that have no real effect on mental health

explanation: Great thinking! Understanding these root causes helps nurses and public health teams focus their support where it's needed most.

question: Which of these is one of Elisabeth Kübler-Ross's classic stages of grief?

options.A: Bargaining
options.B: Isolation
options.C: Revenge
options.D: Forgetfulness

explanation: Spot on! Bargaining is that stage where a person tries to negotiate a different reality. It sits right alongside denial, anger, depression, and acceptance.

question: What type of pathogen causes cholera?

options.A: A virus
options.B: A parasite
options.C: A bacterium
options.D: A fungus

explanation: Cholera is specifically caused by Vibrio cholerae, which is a bacterial infection of the intestinal tract. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T18#GNS313_U2_T18_h1)

question: Why do many patients like to use complementary therapies along with their regular care?

options.A: Because they are always cheaper than conventional drugs
options.B: To replace all standard prescription medications permanently
options.C: To align with personal wellness values and address chronic issues
options.D: Because orthodox doctors mandate them in all hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Patients often look for a whole-person approach that fits their personal beliefs, especially when dealing with long-term health challenges.

question: Why can keeping patient information private be tricky in a home setting?

options.A: Patients demand that all their lab results be broadcasted
options.B: Medical records must be pasted publicly on the front door
options.C: Home health nurses are not legally bound by privacy laws
options.D: Extended family members and neighbors are often present around the living area

explanation: Well reasoned! Open living spaces and bustling family compounds mean we have to be extra careful about who might overhear our discussions.

question: What is the main purpose of development committees in Nigerian primary health care?

options.A: To replace trained doctors in rural clinics
options.B: To encourage community participation and local ownership
options.C: To collect taxes for hospital construction
options.D: To manage federal medical centers directly

explanation: These committees exist to involve local people so they can take charge of their own health needs and partner effectively with health workers. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h1)

question: In Vroom's expectancy theory, what does 'expectancy' actually mean?

options.A: The fear of being punished for a clinical error
options.B: The financial value attached to a year-end bonus
options.C: The belief that effort will lead to successful performance
options.D: The strict rules enforced by the hospital director

explanation: Correct! Expectancy is your personal belief that if you work hard, you will actually succeed at the task.

question: A community health nurse wants to help lower the rate of undiagnosed high blood pressure in a low-income neighborhood. Which activity is the best initial approach?

options.A: Mailing complex research journals to every household in the area
options.B: Instructing residents to buy their own digital blood pressure monitors online
options.C: Waiting inside the hospital clinic for patients to schedule appointments
options.D: Setting up a free mobile blood pressure screening booth at a local community center

explanation: Community outreach brings screening services directly to populations with limited healthcare access, enabling early detection of silent conditions. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h8)

question: Why is fostering community ownership critical for the sustainability of a health intervention?

options.A: It guarantees that all medications will be manufactured locally
options.B: It means nurses no longer need to work in clinics
options.C: It ensures the program survives even after external funding ends
options.D: It allows the community to stop paying taxes permanently

explanation: When a community takes charge of a project, they maintain it independently long after outside financial support stops. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h7)

question: What is the most common bacteria that causes pneumonia outside of the hospital?

options.A: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.B: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.C: Streptococcus pneumoniae
options.D: Influenza virus type A

explanation: Also known simply as pneumococcus, this bug is the leading culprit behind everyday community-acquired pneumonia. Great to keep in mind for clinicals!

question: Why is it super important for nurses in primary health clinics to know about cancer?

options.A: Primary health centers run all national chemotherapy programs
options.B: Infectious diseases are no longer treated in Nigeria
options.C: Community clinics handle complex surgeries daily
options.D: Nurses are usually the first health workers patients see with early symptoms

explanation: Spotting early signs at the grass-roots level means we can refer patients quickly and save lives. Great nursing starts in the community!

question: A patient recovering from laryngeal trauma is ready to start eating again. Which specialist should evaluate them first?

options.A: Registered dietitian
options.B: Speech-language pathologist
options.C: Respiratory therapist
options.D: Physiotherapist

explanation: Great job! A speech-language pathologist specializes in swallowing and must assess the patient to prevent dangerous food aspiration.

question: How long must you listen with a stethoscope in a single part of the tummy before you can safely write down that there are 'no bowel sounds'?

options.A: At least thirty seconds
options.B: A full five minutes
options.C: Until the patient complains
options.D: Exactly one minute

explanation: It takes patience! Bowel sounds can sometimes be very quiet and lazy, so you must listen for a full five minutes in each area before deciding they are truly gone.

question: How is Type 2 diabetes different from Type 1?

options.A: Type 1 can be cured entirely with proper diet and oral medication
options.B: Type 2 only affects elderly individuals who consume high amounts of sugar
options.C: Type 2 involves insulin resistance and relative deficiency rather than complete beta cell destruction
options.D: Type 1 is caused by lifestyle factors while Type 2 is strictly genetic

explanation: In Type 2, the body still makes insulin, but the cells just don't respond to it well (resistance), and the pancreas can't keep up with the extra demand. You're mastering the basics!

question: What exactly is a hospital-acquired complication?

options.A: An expected outcome of chronic disease progression
options.B: A negative health event developing during hospital care
options.C: An illness the patient had before admission
options.D: A normal side effect of curative surgery

explanation: You've got this! These are issues that pop up because a patient is in the healthcare setting or undergoing treatment, rather than being there when they first arrived.

question: What major nutrition paradox do we see in many societies today?

options.A: Vitamin deficiencies have completely disappeared from all populations
options.B: Undernutrition coexists with high rates of obesity and chronic illness
options.C: Everyone in the world now has access to too much food
options.D: People no longer eat carbohydrates or fats anywhere

explanation: You nailed it! It's striking how many communities battle hunger and undernutrition on one side, while fighting lifestyle-related obesity and chronic illness on the other.

question: How does elevated progesterone contribute to digestive discomfort during early pregnancy?

options.A: By relaxing smooth muscle and slowing down digestion
options.B: By increasing the production of strong stomach acids
options.C: By causing the liver to produce excess bile salts
options.D: By speeding up the movement of food through the bowels

explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles all over the body, including the digestive tract, which slows stomach emptying and leads to reflux. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h1)

question: Why are Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Foods (RUTF) so popular for feeding hungry children early in a disaster?

options.A: They have a very short shelf life that forces quick consumption
options.B: They taste sweet and only appeal to adults
options.C: They provide quick nutrition without needing clean cooking water or fuel
options.D: They replace the need for breastfeeding entirely

explanation: When there's no firewood or clean water to cook with, RUTF packets save the day by providing instant, safe nourishment.

question: What is the main goal of a nursing assessment during the menopausal transition?

options.A: To prescribe hormone replacement therapy based on lab values
options.B: To halt the aging process and restore ovarian function
options.C: To evaluate symptom severity, overall health risks, and emotional well-being
options.D: To diagnose underlying psychiatric disorders independently

explanation: As nurses, we look at the whole picture—how symptoms affect her daily life, her health, and her feelings—to give the best support.

question: If a nurse at a rural primary health center diagnoses Lassa fever, who must be notified immediately next in the reporting chain?

options.A: The federal ministry of finance budget office
options.B: The national television broadcasting station
options.C: The Local Government Area surveillance officer
options.D: The World Health Organization headquarters overseas

explanation: Reporting flows step-by-step from the local clinic straight to the Local Government Area (LGA) team before heading to the state and national levels.

question: What causes the shoulder pain some patients feel after a laparoscopic surgery?

options.A: Strain from lifting heavy objects in the recovery room
options.B: Tight bandages applied around the upper chest area
options.C: An awkward position maintained during prolonged walking
options.D: Residual carbon dioxide gas irritating the diaphragm

explanation: Spot on! Leftover gas can press against the diaphragm muscle, tricking the nerves into feeling like the pain is coming from the shoulder.

question: How does climate change directly throw a wrench into farming and crop production?

options.A: Through erratic rainfall, droughts, and rising temperatures
options.B: By making all soils permanently rich and fertile
options.C: Through the complete elimination of all plant pests
options.D: By lowering the global demand for food

explanation: Unpredictable weather, sudden dry spells, and scorching heat mess up traditional planting seasons and ruin harvests.

question: How does the World Health Organization (WHO) define a safe injection?

options.A: One that does not harm the recipient, provider, or community
options.B: One that uses only glass syringes and metal needles
options.C: One that is administered exclusively by registered nurses
options.D: One that costs less than standard oral medications

explanation: Think of the WHO definition as a circle of safety: it covers the patient getting the drug, the nurse giving it, and the public handling the waste.

question: Why is proper documentation of a referral important for the client's care?

options.A: It proves to the government that the nurse worked extra hours
options.B: It prevents the receiving facility from repeating unnecessary assessments
options.C: It allows the nurse to charge extra administrative fees to the client
options.D: It stops the client from ever returning to the primary health center

explanation: Clear notes on clinical history and vital signs save time and guide the receiving team straight to appropriate management. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h5)

question: Why do we place absorbent material inside the secondary packaging of a medical specimen?

options.A: To cushion the glass tubes against heavy outside vibration
options.B: To soak up all the liquid if the primary tube breaks
options.C: To keep the biological specimen frozen during long flights
options.D: To absorb moisture from the humid clinic room air

explanation: It's a built-in safety net! If a tube cracks, the absorbent material traps the fluid so it never leaks outside.

question: In nursing, what does the study of 'epistemology' mainly help us figure out?

options.A: Managing the financial budget of a nursing unit
options.B: Studying how nurses acquire and validate knowledge
options.C: Calculating medication dosages based on body weight
options.D: Mapping out the physical layout of a hospital ward

explanation: Epistemology sounds like a big grammar word, but it just means exploring how we come to know what we know, and how we prove that our nursing care is truly helpful!

question: What is the main focus of Psychological First Aid (PFA) in a disaster?

options.A: Providing humane practical support and reducing distress
options.B: Conducting formal psychoanalysis sessions
options.C: Prescribing strong antidepressant medications
options.D: Diagnosing deep psychiatric disorders

explanation: Well done! PFA isn't about heavy therapy or psychoanalysis; it's about being human, offering practical comfort, and helping people feel safe.

question: A young female is being checked for missing internal reproductive organs. What is the best nursing action during her assessment?

options.A: Reviewing her detailed gynecological and developmental medical history
options.B: Preparing her for immediate emergency abdominal surgery
options.C: Administering oral contraceptives to regulate her menstrual flow
options.D: Instructing her to perform daily bimanual pelvic self-examinations

explanation: Taking a thorough history is a core nursing skill! It helps the team understand whether the issue is congenital or acquired.

question: What is the standard recommended temperature range for storing most routine vaccines in a cold chain?

options.A: Between -10°C and -20°C
options.B: Between +30°C and +40°C
options.C: Between +2°C and +8°C
options.D: Between +15°C and +25°C

explanation: Most routine vaccines lose their potency if allowed to freeze or get too warm, requiring a steady storage range of +2°C to +8°C. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h7)

question: What is the medical term for painful menstrual cramps caused by trapped blood behind scar tissue?

options.A: Dysmenorrhea
options.B: Amenorrhea
options.C: Menorrhagia
options.D: Polymenorrhea

explanation: You got it! Dysmenorrhea means painful periods—and the pain becomes severe when scar tissue blocks menstrual blood from flowing out normally.

question: What is a fomite?

options.A: An inanimate object that can carry and transfer infectious germs
options.B: A living insect that transmits a parasite from animal to human
options.C: A specialized white blood cell that attacks invading bacteria
options.D: A type of protective mask worn during surgical procedures

question: Which communication channel works best when discussing sensitive personal health issues?

options.D: A commercial broadcast on national television

question: What is the main difference between statistical significance and clinical significance in nursing?

options.A: Statistical means the math is real, while clinical means it actually helps the patient

options.C: Clinical significance only matters in laboratories, whereas statistical matters at the bedside
options.D: Statistical significance is based on patient interviews, while clinical uses computers

explanation: You nailed it! Something can be proven by math (statistically significant), but still make barely any noticeable difference to an actual patient in the ward.

question: A Hindu patient asks for a strict vegetarian meal and refuses beef. What is the cultural background for this?

options.A: Hospital kitchens are considered impure by Hindu custom
options.B: Vegetarianism is required only during the winter months
options.C: Cows are viewed as sacred animals, and beef is strictly prohibited
options.D: All animal products are forbidden to prevent spiritual pollution

explanation: In Hinduism, cows hold a very sacred and respected status, making beef consumption a taboo for many observant followers.

question: How do most common drugs cross cell membranes during absorption without using up energy?

options.A: By endocytosis through the engulfing of large molecules
options.B: By active transport using cellular energy stores
options.C: By passive diffusion along a concentration gradient
options.D: By pinocytosis through fluid uptake channels

question: Which type of accident causes the highest number of injuries and trauma on Nigerian roads?

options.A: Road traffic accidents
options.B: Commercial flight crashes
options.C: Skiing and snowboarding falls
options.D: Mountain climbing injuries

question: What is a nurse's legal duty when it comes to suspected child abuse?

options.A: Mediator between parents and social welfare agencies
options.B: Mandated reporter required by law to report suspicions

options.D: Neutral observer who must first confirm absolute proof

question: Why is advocacy so important in primary health care, way beyond just giving treatments?

options.A: It directly cures infectious diseases without medication
options.B: It guarantees immediate government funding for hospitals
options.C: It replaces the need for community health workers
options.D: It addresses systemic barriers that limit healthcare access

explanation: Great thinking! Handing out medications doesn't fix big problems like poverty or bad roads to the clinic. Advocacy tackles those root barriers that keep people from getting care.

question: Why does a grand multiparous woman have a higher risk of her uterus tearing (rupturing) during labor?

options.A: Her baby is usually much smaller than average.
options.B: Her contractions are always weaker than normal.
options.C: Her pelvic bones widen permanently after the first child is born.

question: Expired medications and leftover vaccines belong to which waste category?

options.A: Radioactive waste
options.B: Pharmaceutical waste

options.D: General domestic waste

explanation: You got it! Drugs and medicines always fall under pharmaceutical waste guidelines. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h5)

question: What makes data a 'primary source' in research?

options.A: Data retrieved from older textbooks found in the university library
options.B: Information published in international nursing journals last year
options.C: Patient records stored in the hospital archive from a decade ago
options.D: Information collected firsthand by the researcher for the current study

explanation: Primary data is fresh data you collect yourself right from the source for your own study!

question: What is an essential part of nursing counseling when a couple chooses a traditional family planning method?

options.A: Telling them that partner involvement is unnecessary
options.B: Insisting they switch immediately to surgical sterilization
options.C: Prohibiting them from asking questions about modern drugs
options.D: Discussing the higher risk of failure and backup options

explanation: Good counseling means making sure clients know how well a method actually works so they can plan ahead if a mistake happens.

question: In which direction does a pregnant woman's center of gravity shift as her uterus grows?

options.A: Downward
options.B: Backward
options.C: Forward
options.D: Upward

explanation: The growing uterus and fetus pull the body's weight forward, forcing the mother to adjust her posture to avoid falling. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h2)

question: Why might a newborn infant have slightly swollen breast tissue shortly after birth?

options.A: Early milk production has begun
options.B: Blockage of the lymphatic vessels
options.C: Maternal hormones crossed the placenta
options.D: A congenital infection of the skin

question: Why must gloves be removed before taking off the isolation gown during doffing?

options.A: Because it makes folding the gown easier for laundry
options.B: Because gowns are too heavy to lift with gloves on
options.C: Because gloves are usually the most contaminated item and touched the patient directly
options.D: Because hospital policy forbids touching fabric with latex

explanation: Removing heavily soiled gloves first stops the nurse from accidentally spreading germs from the hands onto the face or clothing while stripping off the gown. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h5)

question: Which symptom is a classic indicator that prompts a doctor to order a fasting blood sugar test?

options.A: Sudden low blood pressure and dizziness
options.B: Excessive thirst and frequent urination
options.C: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles
options.D: Yellowing of the skin and eyes

explanation: Polydipsia and polyuria are hallmark signs of high blood sugar that signal the need for diagnostic screening. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h3)

question: What is a top priority at the bedside for a patient struggling with swallowing due to lower cranial nerve trouble?

options.A: Performing passive range of motion exercises on all extremities
options.B: Applying warm compresses to the forehead to relieve headache
options.C: Keeping mechanical suction equipment ready at the bedside
options.D: Encouraging a high-fiber diet to prevent constipation

explanation: You got this! Patients with trouble swallowing can easily choke or aspirate, so having suction ready keeps them safe.

question: How do pulmonary blood vessels react to an area of the lung that lacks proper ventilation?

options.A: They constrict to redirect blood to better ventilated areas

options.C: They dilate to force more blood into the poorly ventilated alveoli
options.D: They completely shut down the entire right side of the heart

question: Why do planners analyze medical logs and hospital transport times after an event ends?

options.A: To calculate the exact profit margin of the food vendors
