options.C: To evaluate the effectiveness of the medical response and refine future planning
options.D: To verify that all attendees purchased official merchandise

explanation: Looking at medical records helps planners figure out if they had enough nurses, supplies, or ambulances, making future events even safer.

question: When opening a wrapped sterile package on your tray, which flap should you open first?

options.A: The left side flap of the paper wrap
options.B: The right side flap of the paper wrap
options.C: The flap furthest away from the body
options.D: The flap closest to the nurse's chest

explanation: You've got this! Opening the far flap first means your hands won't have to reach directly across the clean items you just exposed. Smart and safe!

question: A ward introduces hourly rounds to stop patient falls. Tracking whether the nurses actually completed those hourly rounds is an example of what?

options.A: Process measure
options.B: Baseline measure
options.C: Balancing measure
options.D: Outcome measure

explanation: Spot on! A process measure simply checks whether the specific steps or tasks in our care plan are actually being carried out day-to-day.

question: What defines a faith-based organization in the health sector?

options.A: It is owned and operated by religious institutions
options.B: It functions exclusively as a commercial pharmacy chain
options.C: It receives all its funding directly from the federal tax board
options.D: It only treats patients who share a specific political view

explanation: Exactly! Faith-based clinics and hospitals are run by religious bodies and provide vital care right in our local communities.

question: What is a major effect of high out-of-pocket user fees on healthcare utilization?

options.A: Hospitals have too much money to spend on equipment.
options.B: Patients seek medical help much earlier in their illness.
options.C: Preventive services are fully utilized by everyone.
options.D: Families delay seeking care until conditions become life-threatening.

explanation: When people have to pay cash directly for every service, they often wait until they are extremely sick before visiting a hospital. [learn more](GST322_U3_T7#GST322_U3_T7_h5)

question: What is the main downside when a nurse suffers from 'under-delegation' (refusing to delegate tasks)?

options.A: Excessive free time for nursing assistants on the ward
options.B: Burnout and exhaustion from trying to perform all tasks personally
options.C: Immediate legal prosecution for negligence by the hospital board
options.D: Complete elimination of patient care errors in the facility

explanation: Trying to do everything yourself on a shift is a fast track to burnout. Trust your team and share the load!

question: Which type of family planning method is generally considered safest for a breastfeeding mother in the early weeks?

options.A: Progestin-only methods
options.B: Emergency morning-after pills
options.C: High-dose estrogen patches
options.D: Combined oral contraceptives

explanation: Progestin-only options (like mini-pills or certain injectables) won't mess with her breastmilk supply, making them a great choice for nursing mums. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h8)

question: A cook uses the same chopping board for raw chicken and fresh tomatoes without washing it first. What just happened?

options.A: Chemical toxicity
options.B: Physical adulteration
options.C: Cross-contamination
options.D: Thermal destruction

explanation: Using dirty equipment between raw meat and fresh veggies easily transfers bacteria from one to the other. Spot on!

question: What happens to the lower oesophageal sphincter in a patient with achalasia?

options.A: It fails to relax properly during swallowing
options.B: It moves upward into the chest cavity
options.C: It dissolves due to lack of local blood supply

question: How do tiny villi and microvilli help the small intestine do its job better?

options.A: By producing strong acid to break down tough plant fibers
options.B: By pushing waste products quickly toward the large bowel
options.C: By greatly increasing the surface area available for absorption
options.D: By storing excess water during times of dehydration

explanation: Brilliant! These tiny finger-like folds give the small intestine a massive surface area so it can soak up as many nutrients as possible.

question: Which antibody class shows up first at the very beginning of a brand-new infection?

options.A: IgA
options.B: IgE
options.C: IgM
options.D: IgG

explanation: Think of IgM as the first responder rushing to the scene! It is always the initial antibody type secreted when your body encounters a brand-new infection.

question: A patient has an infected open leg fracture that hasn't healed over the past eight months, despite short courses of oral antibiotics. What type of osteomyelitis is this?

options.A: Aseptic bone infarction
options.B: Transient bone bruising
options.C: Acute hematogenous osteomyelitis
options.D: Chronic osteomyelitis

question: How do sperm mostly travel upward through the female reproductive tract?

options.A: Riding passively inside the bloodstream after vaginal absorption

options.C: Crawling along the inner walls using specialized cilia

question: How do retinal arterioles typically appear compared to retinal venules during an ophthalmoscopic exam?

options.A: Arterioles are darker red and wider than venules
options.B: Arterioles are brighter red and narrower than venules
options.C: Arterioles and venules look completely identical in color
options.D: Arterioles have no visible blood flow inside them

question: Why is getting too cold (cold stress) so dangerous for a newborn baby?

options.A: It permanently damages sweat gland function
options.B: It lowers peripheral blood pressure to zero
options.C: It causes immediate closure of the ductus arteriosus
options.D: It triggers hypoglycemia and metabolic acidosis

question: As a nurse, what home care instruction should you prioritize for a patient undergoing chemotherapy?

options.A: Stop taking prescribed anti-nausea medications once hair loss begins
options.B: Report a fever or chills immediately to your healthcare provider
options.C: Avoid all physical movement and stay on complete bed rest for weeks
options.D: Restrict fluid intake to prevent abdominal swelling

question: What is the main goal of adding social inclusion into nursing care plans?

options.A: To ensure that all hospital beds are filled by patients from identical backgrounds
options.B: To eliminate the need for physicians to write formal medical prescriptions
options.C: To empower vulnerable patients and reduce health disparities caused by social inequality
options.D: To force patients to change their cultural and religious beliefs before discharge

explanation: Social inclusion in nursing is all about making sure everyone gets fair, respectful care by tackling the root causes of discrimination and helping patients speak for themselves.

question: What is your very first priority action if you suspect a patient is having an idiosyncratic drug reaction?

options.A: Wait for laboratory confirmation before acting
options.B: Increase the drug dose to build up a tolerance
options.C: Give the patient a strong dose of antihistamines
options.D: Stop the offending medication immediately

question: What are the three main categories of immune system dysregulation?

options.B: Hypersensitivity, autoimmunity, and immunodeficiency

options.D: Antibody production, cellular immunity, and innate defense

question: Which of these is the best example of a clear, actionable goal for a nursing unit?

question: What is the official term for the written letter given to a civil servant regarding an alleged workplace offense?

options.A: An APER form

options.D: A query

question: How do target cells commonly bypass receptor-blocking medications?

question: What does it usually mean if a patient's deep tendon reflex is very weak or missing entirely?

question: What is the primary setting targeted by the School Health Programme?

options.D: Educational institutions

question: Why must a baby with a large cephalhematoma be watched closely for jaundice?

question: A nurse is accidentally poked by a needle from a patient who has Hepatitis B. Why is this exposure especially scary?

question: In many Nigerian clinical settings, what is a major hurdle that stops patients from getting their prescribed drugs?

options.A: An oversupply of specialized surgical instruments
options.B: Out-of-pocket spending by patients
options.C: Excessive availability of free hospital parking

question: Why must the middle ear amplify sound vibrations before they pass into the inner ear?

question: What does setting up a 'digital curfew' mean for healthy screen habits?

question: What does the acronym IEC stand for in public health?

options.D: Infection, Evaluation, and Control

question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks comes in with high blood pressure and sudden swelling in her face and hands. What should you suspect?

options.B: Normal physiological edema of pregnancy

question: What is the main focus of an adult day care centre?

options.D: Providing companionship and medication management

question: Which of these items is NOT safe or recommended for hospital waste handlers to wear?

options.C: Sturdy closed shoes or boots
options.D: Protective plastic aprons

question: What is a very common reason new mothers delay their first bowel movement after delivery?

options.B: Severe dehydration that dries out all body fluids
options.C: Complete lack of any urge to defecate for several weeks

question: A fully awake and clear-headed patient says 'No' to a painful procedure. Which ethical principle supports their choice?

options.D: Justice

question: What does the social ecology framework primarily examine when studying adolescent health?

options.D: The financial status of the local healthcare facility

question: Which of the following is NOT a helpful way to encourage eating in a frail older adult?

question: What is the main goal of teamwork between government health structures and NGOs?

options.A: To eliminate the need for community health nurses in rural clinics
options.B: To ensure NGOs take over full ownership of the Ministry of Health
options.C: To increase taxes collected from vulnerable patients

explanation: Working together stops everyone from doing the same job twice! It pools resources so health care reaches more people smoothly.

question: What is the very first step when you want to start a nursing research project?

options.A: Applying for hospital funding
options.B: Collecting patient blood samples
options.C: Identifying the research problem
options.D: Writing the final conclusion

explanation: Every good study starts by figuring out what the exact problem is. You have to spot the gap in patient care before you can start gathering any data!

question: Why do bones break when subjected to excessive physical force?

options.B: Nerves inside the bone stop sending signals
options.C: Blood flow to the bone increases rapidly
options.D: Muscles pull too gently on the joint

question: Which of these is NOT a common negative effect of psychiatric stigma?

options.C: Increased social support and faster recovery times

question: Why must you document a medication immediately after giving it, rather than waiting until the end of your shift?

question: Why do researchers use statistical tables alongside written text in a report?

options.B: Tables summarize precise values so the text can focus on main findings

question: Why is tertiary healthcare so much more expensive to run than primary healthcare?

question: What is the primary hormone responsible for moving glucose from the bloodstream into body cells?

options.C: Glucagon
options.D: Insulin

question: Which scenario represents a violation of the 'right time' medication principle?

question: Who are local community health volunteers primarily expected to help during defaulter tracking?

question: What is the very first practical step when doing medication reconciliation during a home visit?

question: Why do health workers treat gender-based violence as a major public health emergency?

options.B: It primarily places financial strain on hospital pharmacies

question: Why is IEC considered a preventive approach instead of a curative one?

question: What does an HbA1c test measure in a patient with diabetes?

question: What is a key nursing duty during the post-disaster recovery phase?

options.B: Stopping all documentation of past emergency responses
options.C: Discontinuing all community health education programs permanently
options.D: Closing down local clinics indefinitely

explanation: You got it! Even after the dust settles, crowded conditions and dirty water pose major risks, so nurses must stay alert for disease outbreaks.

question: Why is tracking near-expiry drugs important for protecting a DRF?

options.A: It allows the pharmacy to redistribute or discount slow-moving stock before it spoils and wastes money
options.B: It ensures that expired medications can be repackaged with new expiration dates
options.C: It forces the manufacturer to refund the hospital for drugs that sell too quickly
options.D: It proves to the patients that the hospital only buys the freshest imported drugs

explanation: Catching drugs before they expire lets you transfer them or sell them off, saving the facility from losing hard-earned capital.

question: When is the very first (baseline) needle count done during a procedure?

options.A: When the patient is rolling out of the recovery room
options.B: After the surgeon has closed the skin incision
options.C: Before the surgery begins during instrument setup
options.D: Only when an emergency X-ray is requested

explanation: Fantastic! We always do a baseline count before any cut is made so we know exactly what we started with. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h3)

question: What does the term ' hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy' mean?

options.A: Brain injury resulting from lack of oxygen and blood flow
options.B: A chronic skin rash caused by poor circulation
options.C: Sudden kidney failure due to low fluid volume
options.D: An infection of the lining surrounding the lungs

explanation: Break it down: 'hypoxic' (low oxygen), 'ischemic' (low blood flow), 'encephalopathy' (brain disease/injury). You've mastered a big medical term!

question: Why is the community health planning cycle described as continuous and circular?

options.A: The exact same health problem must be treated over and over again
options.B: Evaluation findings lead directly into the next round of assessment and planning
options.C: It must be repeated every thirty days regardless of community needs
options.D: Healthcare workers rotate through different villages in a fixed circle

explanation: Because health needs change and programs must adapt, the end of one evaluation simply sparks the beginning of the next planning phase. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h1)

question: What does a very small standard deviation mean for a set of patient temperature readings?

options.A: The readings are closely clustered near the average temperature
options.B: The highest temperature reading was far above normal limits
options.C: There was a major calculation error made during data entry
options.D: The patients have completely different underlying health conditions

explanation: A small standard deviation means everyone's readings are hugging close to the average—very little variation!

question: Why do doctors sometimes combine a potassium-sparing diuretic with a loop diuretic?

options.A: To completely stop the patient from urinating at night
options.B: To replace the need for measuring blood pressure
options.C: To prevent the low potassium levels caused by loop diuretics
options.D: To speed up how fast the kidneys filter blood

explanation: It's all about balance! Loop diuretics waste potassium, while potassium-sparing ones hold onto it. Pairing them keeps the patient's electrolytes steady.

question: Why is twisting your body while lifting a heavy patient a big risk?

options.A: It puts uneven stress on the spinal discs
options.B: It cuts off circulation in the legs
options.C: It immediately lowers the patient's blood pressure
options.D: It causes the nurse to drop the patient's legs

explanation: Twisting while carrying weight puts awkward pressure on your spine, which is a quick way to get a bad back injury. Always pivot with your feet instead!

question: A patient keeps getting severe bacterial infections. Which lab values should the nurse check first to see how their antibody defenses are doing?

options.A: Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
options.B: Serum immunoglobulin levels (IgG, IgA, IgM)
options.C: Liver enzymes (ALT and AST)
options.D: Fasting serum cholesterol and lipids

explanation: Immunoglobulins (antibodies) handle our humoral immunity. Checking IgG, IgA, and IgM levels helps us see if an antibody shortage is leaving the patient wide open to infections.

question: What are the two major muscle problems seen in a patient with achalasia?

options.A: Premature contraction of the diaphragm and paralysis of the phrenic nerve
options.B: Weakness of the upper sphincter and rapid food transit into the duodenum
options.C: Constant spasm of the upper sphincter and excessive stomach acid production
options.D: Failure of the lower sphincter to relax and lack of normal peristalsis

explanation: Brilliant! In achalasia, the food pipe forgets how to push food down properly (no peristalsis), and the bottom valve stubbornly stays clamped shut.

question: What is the main goal of laws and policies guiding waste disposal in healthcare?

options.A: To generate revenue through heavy facility fines
options.B: To make hospital paperwork as complicated as possible
options.C: To restrict the purchase of medical equipment
options.D: To standardize safe practices and protect public safety

explanation: You got it! Laws ensure every clinic and hospital follows clear, uniform rules to keep staff and patients safe.

question: What is the main goal that drives voluntary health agencies?

options.A: Replacing public hospitals completely
options.B: Generating high commercial profits
options.C: Humanitarian values and public service
options.D: Enforcing strict government tax laws

explanation: You got this! Voluntary agencies are non-profits driven by community welfare and helping others rather than chasing financial gain.

question: A cleaner uses the same trolley to carry food trays in the morning and infectious waste in the afternoon. What went wrong here?

options.A: The cleaner failed to wear heavy-duty rubber gloves and aprons
options.B: Cross-contamination risks have been created between waste and food
options.C: The temporary storage room was kept too cold and well-ventilated
options.D: The infectious waste bags were tied too tightly before transport

explanation: Spot on! Using the same equipment for food and waste spreads dangerous germs all over the hospital.

question: Why is writing prompt and accurate patient notes so important in home health care?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for verbal handovers to colleagues
options.B: It stops family members from asking questions about the patient
options.C: It serves as your legal proof of the care and assessments you provided
options.D: It guarantees you will get paid on time by health insurance

explanation: Exactly! In nursing, if it wasn't charted, it wasn't done. Good notes protect both you and the patient.

question: Why do researchers run a pilot test before the main study starts?

options.A: To identify confusing questions and logistical flaws on a small scale
options.B: To force hospital administrators to approve the study immediately
options.C: To publish the final research paper ahead of all other researchers
options.D: To replace the need for formal ethical clearance from the review board

explanation: A pilot test is like a dress rehearsal. It helps you catch messy questions or flaws before you roll out the full study.

question: Why is exact timing so important for blood draws during dynamic hormone tests?

options.A: Blood samples spoil if they sit at room temperature
options.B: Hormones disappear from the blood after five minutes
options.C: Laboratory technicians only work during morning hours
options.D: Hormone levels shift rapidly in response to specific triggers

explanation: Hormones react fast! Precise timing lets us catch the exact moment the gland reacts to our test medicine.

question: Why is it important to involve bedside nurses when drafting clinical standards?

options.A: They perform the actual care and understand practical floor realities
options.B: It guarantees that hospital funding will increase
options.C: It removes the need for any supervisory oversight
options.D: They are the only ones allowed to sign administrative policies

explanation: Frontline nurses know what works in daily practice, making their input vital for creating realistic and usable standards. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h4)

question: What is the primary focus of microbiology?

options.A: The chemical composition of human blood
options.B: The electrical signals of the nervous system
options.C: The study of microscopic living organisms
options.D: The physical structure of human bones

explanation: Microbiology specifically investigates organisms too small to be seen clearly with the naked eye. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h1)

question: A nurse working in a rural primary health clinic notices an increase in skin infections among children. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Close the clinic permanently until a modern hospital is built nearby
options.B: Investigate local hygiene practices and provide health education on hand washing
options.C: Order expensive laboratory tests from overseas for every sick child
options.D: Tell parents that skin infections cannot be prevented in rural areas

explanation: The nurse begins by assessing the community's hygiene habits and teaching simple, effective prevention strategies to stop the outbreak. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h8)

question: During which step of Psychological First Aid (PFA) does a nurse help a survivor reach loved ones and community help?

options.A: Lock
options.B: Link
options.C: Listen
options.D: Look

explanation: Brilliant! The 'Link' step is all about connecting people back to their support systems, family members, and helpful community resources. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h5)

question: What happens when the internal urethral sphincter relaxes during normal urination?

options.A: The kidneys immediately start producing a fresh batch of urine.
options.B: Semen is forced backward into the bladder instead of moving forward.
options.C: The pelvic floor muscles contract violently to push out the remaining waste.
options.D: Urine is allowed to flow out of the bladder into the upper urethra.

explanation: Spot on! Relaxing this internal muscle opens the bladder neck so urine can begin its journey down.

question: At approximately what urine volume do most adults first feel a conscious desire to void?

options.A: 1000 to 1500 milliliters
options.B: 2000 to 2500 milliliters
options.C: 50 to 100 milliliters
options.D: 200 to 400 milliliters

explanation: Stretch receptors begin signaling the brain strongly once bladder volume reaches roughly 200 to 400 milliliters. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h5)

question: In a research study, what do we call the 'independent variable'?

options.A: The total number of patients who refused to participate
options.B: The intervention or cause manipulated by the researcher
options.C: The final outcome measured at the end of the project
options.D: The random error that occurs during data collection

explanation: You got it! The independent variable is the active ingredient or change that the researcher introduces to see what happens.

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge to eating a diverse diet in Nigeria?

options.A: Seasonal changes that affect fresh crop yields
options.B: Cultural taboos restricting certain foods for mothers
options.C: High market prices and general household poverty
options.D: Excessive availability of free vitamin supplements

explanation: Correct! Free supplements are a good thing, not a barrier. Poverty, seasonal shifts, and strict food customs are the real hurdles families face.

question: Which core principle of community health nursing is all about fairness and helping vulnerable groups first?

options.A: Rigid institutional control
options.B: Medical dominance
options.C: Hospital centralization
options.D: Equity in care

explanation: Well done! Equity means making sure resources go where they are needed most so everyone has a fair chance at good health.

question: How does unit dispensing improve financial transparency for patients?

options.A: Medication prices are standardized across all states
options.B: Hospital care becomes completely free of charge
options.C: Invoices are calculated based on hospital stay duration
options.D: Patients pay only for the exact doses administered

explanation: Instead of buying an entire pack of fifty tablets when only five are needed, the patient only pays for those five doses. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting quality improvement reviews in a rehab facility?

options.A: To identify safety risks and find ways to improve patient care outcomes
options.B: To increase the cost of hospital admission fees
options.C: To find individual staff members to punish for making mistakes
options.D: To reduce the number of therapy hours required by insurance

explanation: Spot on! Quality improvement is all about making systems safer and patient care better—it's never about assigning blame.

question: Which of these is a reliable way for a nurse to check if a patient is really taking their drugs?

options.A: Conducting pill counts and reviewing pharmacy refill logs
options.B: Trusting that the patient remembers all dosing schedules accurately
options.C: Assuming compliance if the patient smiles during clinic visits
options.D: Asking family members if they think the patient looks healthy

explanation: Numbers don't lie! Pill counts and pharmacy records give us solid proof of whether the medicine is actually leaving the container.

question: Why should a nurse assess a patient's swallowing ability before giving oral pills?

options.A: To prevent choking and potential aspiration into the lungs
options.B: To see if the patient has any food allergies
options.C: To check how fast the liver will metabolize the drug
options.D: To determine if the patient prefers liquid or solid medicines

explanation: Swallowing difficulties place patients at high risk of aspirating foreign objects or liquids into the respiratory tract. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h4)

question: What does the letter 'M' stand for in the TNM cancer staging system?

options.A: Muscle involvement
options.B: Microscopic grading
options.C: Distant metastasis
options.D: Malignant potential

explanation: Spot on! In the TNM system, M tells us if the cancer has traveled (metastasized) to distant organs far away from where it started.

question: Why is it important to respect a patient's cultural background when planning their meals?

options.A: Because medical science proves cultural foods are superior
options.B: To prevent the client from ever eating carbohydrates
options.C: Because hospital policy strictly forbids serving foreign foods
options.D: To ensure the client is willing and able to follow the meal plan long-term

explanation: People eat what they love! When we respect cultural food preferences, patients are much more likely to stick to their diet.

question: How do conditions like a stroke often lead to urinary incontinence?

options.A: They cause the kidneys to produce excessive amounts of urine
options.B: They permanently shrink the overall size of the bladder
options.C: They destroy the lining of the urinary tract
options.D: They disrupt nerve signals between the brain and the bladder

explanation: Our brain and spinal cord need to talk to the bladder to control peeing. When a stroke damages those pathways, that communication gets mixed up.

question: A patient arrives at a primary health clinic with a severe postpartum hemorrhage that requires a blood transfusion. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Send the patient home with oral pain relievers
options.B: Stabilize the patient and quickly arrange transfer to a CEmONC facility
options.C: Perform a major surgical operation right there in the primary clinic
options.D: Wait for the bleeding to stop on its own before taking action

explanation: Basic clinics cannot handle blood transfusions or major surgery, so quick stabilization and emergency referral are mandatory. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h5)

question: A patient's waste moves through the colon at a normal speed, but they still struggle with hard stools and straining because of their diet. What do we call this type of constipation?

options.A: Slow-transit constipation
options.B: Normal-transit constipation
options.C: Mechanical bowel obstruction
options.D: Pelvic floor dysfunction

explanation: Even when the gut moves at a normal speed, everyday things like not eating enough fiber or drinking less water can cause normal-transit constipation. Easy peasy once you break it down!

question: Why is using an AED as quickly as possible so important during cardiac arrest?

options.A: It automatically contacts the local police department for help
options.B: It permanently cures any underlying heart disease causing the arrest
options.C: It replaces the need to ever perform chest compressions
options.D: Survival rates drop significantly with every minute that defibrillation is delayed

explanation: Every single minute counts! Without blood flow, the brain quickly loses oxygen, so acting fast truly saves lives.

question: Which complication of long bone fractures (like the femur) involves breathing trouble and a spotty rash?

options.A: Fat embolism syndrome
options.B: Osteomyelitis infection
options.C: Superficial skin breakdown
options.D: Chronic bone spur formation

explanation: Fat droplets from inside the bone marrow can slip into the bloodstream after a long bone break, traveling to the lungs and brain. Watch out for breathing issues and a petechial rash!

question: What happens when surviving nephrons have to overwork because their neighbors broke down?

options.A: They regenerate completely to cure the disease
options.B: They stop working immediately to rest the kidney
options.C: They turn into normal liver cells
options.D: They undergo hyperfiltration and suffer further damage

explanation: Think of it like carrying extra load—when healthy nephrons take over for damaged ones, the heavy workload puts them under stress, wearing them out faster too.

question: What is an important thing to remember when looking at a low serum albumin level in a sick patient?

options.A: Albumin also drops during inflammation, which can look like malnutrition
options.B: Albumin only measures fluid intake
options.C: Albumin levels always spike right after a high-fat meal
options.D: Lab errors make albumin completely useless in hospitals

explanation: Infection and body stress trigger inflammation, which lowers albumin levels even if the patient's diet is fine. Keep this in mind during clinicals!

question: Which body position is most commonly used to prepare a patient for an intrathecal injection?

options.A: Supine position with legs elevated at 45 degrees
options.B: Trendelenburg position with a pillow under the head
options.C: Prone position with arms extended overhead
options.D: Lateral decubitus with knees drawn up to the chest

explanation: Curling into a tight fetal position arches the back and widens the gaps between vertebrae for easier needle access. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h5)

question: A patient living in a food desert with no personal car is most likely to buy food from where?

options.A: Large wholesale farmers markets in the city center
options.B: Local corner convenience stores and fast-food outlets
options.C: Specialty butcher shops selling lean grass-fed meats
options.D: Community gardens growing organic leafy greens

explanation: Without transport to large supermarkets, people living in food deserts rely heavily on nearby corner shops and fast food. Keep up the good work!

question: A family's well water is muddy with visible dirt particles. What should they do first before treating it?

options.A: Boil the muddy water without any preparation
options.B: Drink the water quickly before particles dissolve
options.C: Allow the water to undergo sedimentation
options.D: Add large amounts of liquid bleach immediately

explanation: Spot on! Letting the heavy dirt settle to the bottom first (sedimentation) makes cleaning or boiling the water much more effective.
